requirement: `habeas status [<selection>] [--all] [--verbose]` MUST consider requirements and named examples matched by the {term}`requirements.references.definition_selection`; without a selection it MUST consider every definition. By default, it MUST list matching definitions in full-name order when their evidence is missing, has a false determination, or fails the same evidence and reference checks as `habeas::validate()`. It MUST summarize FIXME judgments under {cite}`requirements.cli.fixme_summary`, with accepted FIXME subjects listed individually only when `--verbose` or `--all` is selected. `--all` MUST list every matching definition with its kind and evidence state. Every form MUST show validation findings, work from within a Cargo and mdBook project, and report invalid arguments or a supplied selection matching no definition clearly. Every form MUST also list, in a "Disagreements" section, each selected definition, citation review, and site review whose recorded rationale states that its assessments disagreed under {cite}`requirements.authoring.confirmation.disagreement`, regardless of whether validation accepts the recorded judgment.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.cli.status` states only observable behavior, so it has no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence. It has no implementation edges and no review roots were supplied.

I checked each candidate clause for a structural reading:
- **Command form** (`habeas status [<selection>] [--all] [--verbose]`): this is the command-line syntax. Any parser that accepts and rejects the same arguments behaves identically. The text names no argument-parsing library.
- **Selection** ("matched by the definition selection"; "without a selection it MUST consider every definition"): this fixes which definitions are chosen. It does not fix how they are chosen.
- **Default listing** ("list matching definitions in full-name order when their evidence is missing, has a false determination, or fails the same evidence and reference checks as `habeas::validate()`"): this is the closest candidate. An alternative that re-implements the same checks, or reuses them some other way, produces identical output. The clause requires the same outcomes, not a call to a named function, so I read it as behavioral.
- **FIXME summary**, **`--all`**, **validation findings**, **working from within a Cargo and mdBook project**, **clear error reporting**, and the **"Disagreements" section**: each describes output content, ordering or a failure condition. Each can be met by any internal structure.

The cited requirements `requirements.cli.fixme_summary` and `requirements.authoring.confirmation.disagreement` supply context only. They are also behavioral: grouping and counting rules, and what a rationale must record. The definition `requirements.references.definition_selection` is vocabulary only.

No implementation evidence is needed here. Whether the tests cover the behavior belongs to the behavioral criterion.

behavioral: I found no test gap for `requirements.cli.status`. I did not need implementation source. Each obligation maps to tests as follows.

- **Selection and default scope:**
  - `tests/commands.rs#fn[status_and_info_accept_a_definition_selection]` checks that `requirements.c*` with `--all` shows `requirements.case` and excludes `requirements.ready`. It also checks the help text for the selection argument.
  - `commands_report_invalid_arguments_and_unmatched_selectors` checks that `requirements.*ready` selects `ready` and `xready` and excludes `pending`.
  - Plain `status` with no selection is the default in `status_lists_nonvalid_requirements_and_all_option_in_name_order`.
  - `verbose_status_lists_fixme_judgments_and_globs_scope_issue_groups` checks selection with `rules.case` and `rules.unlinked`.
  - An exact name selects only that definition. `status_applies_workspace_disallow_to_existing_evidence` selects `requirements.ready`, and `status_retains_repository_findings_without_indexing_unreferenced_functions` does the same.
- **Default listing in full-name order:** `status_lists_nonvalid_requirements_and_all_option_in_name_order` covers each condition:
  - Missing evidence: `absent`.
  - False determination: `pending`.
  - Validation failures: `malformed`, `stale` (requirement text changed), `stale_input` (outline input changed) and `uncovered` (no input covers).
  - Valid definitions are absent from the default listing.
  - The default list is in name order.
- **Reference and evidence checks matching `habeas::validate()`:**
  - `status_applies_workspace_disallow_to_existing_evidence` checks a disallowed path.
  - `working_directory_references_count_immediately_and_follow_nested_ignore_rules` checks that a reference finding reaches status output.
  - `completed_inadequate_expiration_review_is_current_and_reported_by_status` checks a false determination.
- **FIXME summary and verbose listing:**
  - `status_groups_fixme_judgments_by_distinct_exact_issue` checks that accepted FIXME subjects are not listed by default and appear in `--all`.
  - `verbose_status_lists_fixme_judgments_and_globs_scope_issue_groups` checks that `--verbose` lists them.
  - `valid_fixme_remains_visible_in_status_info_and_book` checks `status_markdown` for both `all` values and for verbose. It asserts `requirements.timeout` appears only when `all` is set or verbose is used, and that no validation findings appear.
  - The grouping details belong to `requirements.cli.fixme_summary`, which is cited rather than reassessed. Those tests also apply it here.
- **`--all` listing:** `status_lists_nonvalid_requirements_and_all_option_in_name_order` checks the kind (`(example)`), the state (`Valid`), name order and the presence of `ready` and `xready`. `valid_fixme_remains_visible_in_status_info_and_book` checks the `FIXME` state cell.
- **Validation findings in every form:** `status_retains_repository_findings_without_indexing_unreferenced_functions` runs default, `--all`, `--verbose` and `--all --verbose`, each with and without a selection, from a nested directory. It asserts the `invalid JSON` finding every time. `status_loads_nearest_workspace_file_without_validating_authoring` checks the findings for an invalid workspace file.
- **Working from within a Cargo and mdBook project:**
  - The tests run from `src/nested`, and the nearest workspace file is used.
  - `commands_report_invalid_arguments_and_unmatched_selectors` checks the clear error outside a project: `cannot find a project with Cargo.toml and book.toml`.
- **Invalid arguments and unmatched selections reported clearly:**
  - `commands_report_invalid_arguments_and_unmatched_selectors` checks the usage text on stderr for `--wrong` and extra arguments, `invalid definition glob` for `[`, and `no definitions match` for `nothing.*`.
  - `obsolete_status_coverage_flag_is_rejected_with_usage` checks that the obsolete `--coverage` flag is rejected.
- **Disagreements section:** `src/commands.rs#mod[tests]/fn[status_lists_definitions_and_reviews_whose_assessments_disagreed]` covers this obligation.
  - It records a definition, a site review and a citation review whose assessments disagreed, plus non-disagreeing counterparts (`requirements.other` and `check_one`).
  - It checks the exact rows in default, `--all` and `--verbose` modes, and with selections `requirements.rule` and `requirements.other`.
  - It asserts that the non-disagreeing items are excluded.
  - It shows the section appears even when validation rejects the definition's false determination. It also shows the section is omitted when no selected item disagrees.
  - `--all` and `--verbose` together are not combined in this test. The text distinguishes no behavior for that pair, so I do not count it as a gap.

The tests assert the outcomes, not only that they run. No acknowledgments were present or needed.

text: :::{req} status

`habeas status [<selection>] [--all] [--verbose]` MUST consider requirements and named examples matched by the {term}`requirements.references.definition_selection`; without a selection it MUST consider every definition. By default, it MUST list matching definitions in full-name order when their evidence is missing, has a false determination, or fails the same evidence and reference checks as `habeas::validate()`. It MUST summarize FIXME judgments under {cite}`requirements.cli.fixme_summary`, with accepted FIXME subjects listed individually only when `--verbose` or `--all` is selected. `--all` MUST list every matching definition with its kind and evidence state. Every form MUST show validation findings, work from within a Cargo and mdBook project, and report invalid arguments or a supplied selection matching no definition clearly. Every form MUST also list, in a "Disagreements" section, each selected definition, citation review, and site review whose recorded rationale states that its assessments disagreed under {cite}`requirements.authoring.confirmation.disagreement`, regardless of whether validation accepts the recorded judgment.
:::{req} fixme_summary
`habeas status` MUST group the selected requirement and example judgments marked
FIXME by issue reference and report how many distinct judgments each issue
affects. A recorded FIXME string of the form `owner/repo#N` under
{cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes` MUST identify that issue, compared exactly; any
other string is a gap description without an issue.
A judgment MUST count at most once for each issue, even when that issue occurs
repeatedly or in several FIXME strings. A judgment naming several issues MUST
count in each corresponding group. Judgments with no issue string MUST be counted once in a separate "FIXME without an issue" group.
Issue groups MUST be ordered by decreasing affected-judgment count, then by
reference; the group without an issue MUST follow them. A supplied
selection MUST restrict these counts to the selected subjects.
`--verbose` MUST list the full name and kind of every judgment in each issue
group and in the group without an issue, along with its original FIXME strings.
The summary MUST include valid FIXME determinations even when other evidence
checks fail; grouping MUST NOT hide their validation findings. Malformed
determinations MUST remain validation errors under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`.
:::{req} confirmation.disagreement
When two assessments differ in judgment kind or site applicability, the evidence
rationale MUST report both decisions, their explanations, and which decision was
recorded under {cite}`requirements.authoring.confirmation.selection`.
{cite}`requirements.cli.flip_guidance`
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
